card.name: Odissi
card.era: Ancient roots (2nd-c BCE evidence); revived mid-20th c
card.tagline: Odisha's lyrical temple classical dance of tribhanga and chowk
card.profile: Odissi (formerly Orissi) is an ancient Indian classical dance that originated in the temples of Odisha, performed predominantly by women to express religious stories, especially of Vaishnavism (Wikipedia). Its technique is built around the chowk (a square, masculine stance) and the tribhanga (a feminine three-bend posture), with fluid movements and emphasis on bhakti bhava (devotion) (Britannica). Theoretical roots trace to the Natya Shastra's Odra-Magadhi style, with dance poses evidenced in the Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves and temple sculptures at Konark and Puri (Wikipedia).
card.insight: Historically sustained by Mahari temple dancers and Gotipua boy dancers, Odissi was reconstructed and won Sangeet Natak Akademi recognition in the late 1950s through gurus such as Kelucharan Mohapatra and Pankaj Charan Das (Sahapedia).
